findings.kind: new lower location of retained cache-contract issue
findings.mismatch: Compiled once and arbitrary concurrent use overstates cache/concurrency contract. Cache misses build outside map lock and may race; module compilation mutex does not recheck the cache after waiting.
findings.remedy: Say instances share compiled successful kernel outcomes through their cache. Concurrent misses can compile more than once. Independent operations may share the device; resource/mapping ownership remains caller-controlled.
findings.acceptance: No exactly-once or arbitrary shared-resource safety promise; native policy/device keys and possible races described consistently with canonical cache.

findings.kind: new lower location of retained std scope rationale issue
findings.mismatch: Cross-thread error-scope interleaving rationale is false under explicit native std. Constructor obtains all six kernels, but thread-local scopes do not prove later compilation must be prohibited.
findings.remedy: State the constructor obtains all six compiled handles from the shared cache and later bakes use them; remove the cross-thread scope explanation.
findings.acceptance: Native std thread-local SDK contract retained without exactly-once or unsupported performance claims.

findings.mismatch: Armor scratch says bytes bytes but rounds to at least four. Metal scratch currently takes native u32 words and rounds to at least one word; those input units are not interchangeable.
findings.remedy: Document the retained minimum four-byte scalar allocation and explicit byte-vs-word boundary. Consume canonical byte length through repaired internal APIs; convert authored word layouts exactly once.
findings.acceptance: One shared BufferByteLength owner; no duplicate quantity/compatibility overload. Every connected producer migrated with min-four behavior explicit.

findings.mismatch: Buffer read has no API docs and facade wording implies unconditional finished writing. Correct readback requires same logical device/queue, producing submissions handled before mapping, and exclusive ownership of any externally mappable source during map/unmap.
findings.remedy: Document logical byte-prefix result, typed host-layout admission, staging vs direct mapping, native blocking progress vs browser callback await, context provenance and external unmapped/exclusive mapping preconditions. Describe completion of this readback, not future concurrent submissions or all GPU work.
findings.acceptance: Docs match repaired success/error cleanup; no promise of universal runtime safety, rollback or capturing device-handled native errors.

findings.mismatch: Only-already-mappable explanation for missing callback is stronger than established native callback contract. Poll results are discarded. Core extracts closures under synchronization and fires them afterwards, so thread-shared progress needs no exclusive causal claim.
findings.remedy: Describe driving device progress until mapping result delivery; propagate actual polling errors. Remove portable Windows timing attribution unless a bounded measurement is documented separately.
findings.acceptance: Wait snapshot at poll start, callback delivery and typed poll/map/channel causes remain distinct; no inevitable watchdog or latency claim.

findings.mismatch: Every read waits for the queue and after everything submitted so far are unqualified across native/browser/direct-mappable paths. Current staging ignores submit Result and retains old peer Readback arity.
findings.remedy: Document one grouped staging mapping in recorded source order, successful producing-batch helper result prerequisite and separate native wait/browser callback completion. Adopt peer record(batch,sources)/read() API and propagate submit before mapping.
findings.acceptance: Retained actual device supplies allocation/polling; helper Ok policy-relative, no final global queue/GPU verdict.

findings.kind: new lower error classification mismatch; implementation source-loss already retained
findings.mismatch: Device failure cannot recover classification is too broad for parser/admission/host-layout/map/allocation errors. Current helpers stringify concrete errors, so API carriers lose source.
findings.remedy: Describe converting a failed GPU-backed operation with its underlying cause. Implement agreed GenerateError::Gpu(anyhow source), Metal anyhow with focused operation context, Buffer read anyhow; retain existing distinct Skin/Readback/PlateShell causes.
findings.acceptance: Real native, map, poll, channel, address/allocation causes remain discoverable; display prefixes remain contextual, not claimed runtime device-loss diagnosis.

findings.kind: new lower caller-owned token and decoding contract
findings.mismatch: Staged ordinal and generic get/status docs omit that token must come from corresponding staging result, bytes must encode complete T records, and status needs a word. Prefix truncates at most count and cannot prove logical length/type.
findings.remedy: If those APIs remain caller-owned, document token/result correspondence, typed decoding and nonempty status requirements explicitly; describe prefix as at most count. Reconcile any source invariant repair in root inventory rather than merely claiming checked admission.
findings.acceptance: No documentation claim that naked ordinal/Pod admits cross-result identity or a guaranteed exact prefix.
